title: Wagon cup holder: v3, cup lifts off the clip
subtitle: Clip stays on the right-hand side rail · the cup module drops onto a dovetail and lifts straight off · shown assembled, in print orientation · millimetres
scale_note: Real size, shown assembled. The rail is your 22.3 mm tube (assumed the same on the side rail). The tumbler is from retailer listings (70 mm base, 89 mm widest), not your cup. It is drawn in print orientation: the rail axis is vertical here and the cup lies on its side. In use the rail is horizontal and the cup stands upright, hanging off the outside of it. To take the cup off, the module lifts straight up along the dovetail.
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v3: you need the cup off quickly for folding, so it is now two pieces. The clip (the ring with the ears and bolt) is tightened once with a hex key and stays on the rail. The cup module drops down onto the clip's dovetail, rests on the ear tops, and lifts straight off with the cup in it, one-handed, no tool. Toggle the pieces to see them apart. What stays on the rail is the clip: 70 mm long, about 28 mm above the rail axis, 24 mm below, 22 mm outboard and 18 mm inboard. Please check: (1) does that empty clip get in the way when you fold the wagon? Clamp the 15 mm test slice on the right rail and fold it. (2) is the red latch or the diagonal strut outboard of the rail in that zone? If so the module's web will hit it. (3) measure your tumbler's base and widest diameter. Then print the three small test pieces: the clamp slice and the dovetail pair.
